Hi Maya — great to hear, excited to get Skylabs onboarded. Below is a concise provisioning plan and checklist we typically follow for Dedicated GPU pools. I'm copying Laura (CSM, onboarding lead) and Marcus (Infra) to start scheduling the intake and capacity validation.

Redwood Dedicated - Initial provisioning checklist (high level)
- Confirm committed capacity: GPU type (A100/H100), vGPU count, target concurrent requests (you specified ~120 concurrent users), peak tokens/sec estimate
- Region selection: primary us-west, failover us-east — confirm data residency and any network restrictions
- Network setup: VPC peering / PrivateLink options, egress rules, IP allowlist
- Autoscaling & burst policy: target latency SLO (p95 in ms), min/max pool size, burst buffer config (minutes of burst), pre-warm strategy for scheduled events
- Caching/batching defaults: prefix caching for stable prompts, KV cache size considerations for session-based chat
- Security & compliance: KMS integration or bring-your-own-key, audit log retention window, SOC2 evidence needs
- SOW & procurement items: SOW draft, billing contact, procurement PO cadence, required SLAs
- Kickoff & cutover plan: intake call, environment provisioning, test workload run, canary traffic shift, go-live date

Suggested timeline (typical):
- Day 0: SOW signed + PO received
- Day 1-3: Network config + account setup
- Day 4-7: GPU pool provisioning and base image deploy
- Day 8-10: Performance validation (load test + latency verification)
- Day 11-14: Canary rollout and QA -> go-live

Action items for Skylabs (please):
1) Confirm GPU preference (A100 vs H100) and any procurement constraints
2) Approve region failover plan (us-west primary, us-east failover)
3) Share a representative workload trace or token/sec estimate for sizing
4) Review attached SOW draft (I attached v1) and provide billing contact for PO

Laura & Marcus — can you propose two 30-min slots for an intake call tomorrow or Thursday?

Best,
David Kim
